samples.summary: XLSX importer's new merge-budget enforcement has no test
samples.evidence: `applyMergeRanges` now accumulates a `MergeBudget` and silently `continue`s on merges the budget refuses (xlsx-importer.ts:250-277). Grepping packages/sheets/test/import/xlsx-importer.test.ts for 'merge' finds only the pre-existing single `<mergeCell ref="A1:B1"/>` fixture (line 59) and its assertion (line 103); no fixture exercises an over-budget file, and nothing asserts that affordable merges keep loading once the running budget is incremented. A wiring bug (e.g. the running total never incremented, or the whole map dropped after the first refusal) would be invisible: a large real workbook could import with merges silently missing, or an untrusted file could still write a map the load walk cannot afford.
searchedFor: grep 'mergeBudget' across packages/sheets (only src + merge.test.ts helper-level tests)
glob packages/sheets/test/**/*.ts for an importer budget test

samples.summary: canMergeSelection's map-level budget (`this.mergeBudget`) is never exercised; the only test trips the per-span cap instead
samples.evidence: The new field `mergeBudget` (sheet.ts:340, set in rebuildMergeCoverMap:916) is consulted at sheet.ts:4931. The only test, merge.test.ts:46-52 ('refuses a selection the budget cannot afford'), selects a span of MaxMergedCells+1 cells, which `mergeBudgetAdmits` rejects on the per-span check alone — it returns false even if `this.mergeBudget` were permanently `{entries:0, coveredCells:0}`. No test merges a small selection on a sheet whose existing map is already at MaxMergeEntries/MaxMergeCoveredCells, so a bug that never accumulates or never refreshes `mergeBudget` would pass the suite while letting the editor grow the map past what the load-time walk can afford.

samples.summary: `sortFilterByColumn` clearing the copy buffer is untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds `this.clearCopyBuffer()` in `sortFilterByColumn` (sheet.ts:4076-4082) as one of the four renumbering paths. merge.test.ts covers insert (line ~197), reorder (~217) and undo/redo (~1389), but grepping `getCopyRange|clearCopyBuffer` across packages/sheets/test shows no hit in filter.test.ts, whose four `sortFilterByColumn` calls (filter.test.ts:203,226,260,325) assert nothing about the clipboard. If the call is dropped, a paste after a sort relocates formulas and re-creates merged blocks from stale coordinates — the exact data corruption the other three calls are tested against.

samples.summary: View-level wiring of the new refusal/copy-buffer behavior is untested
samples.evidence: Three view-level behaviors change with no test: the drag-reorder handler now bails out of re-selecting when `moveRows/moveColumns` return false (worksheet.ts:4661-4667), the paste handlers no longer call `clearCopyBuffer` (worksheet.ts:~4947, spreadsheet.ts:~724), and `revalidateCopyBuffer` is now invoked on remote change (worksheet.ts:5248). The engine-level counterparts are tested in merge.test.ts (moveRows returning false, repeat internal paste, revalidateCopyBuffer called directly), but nothing under packages/sheets/test/view exercises the wiring — a missed `if (!moved) return` or a missing `revalidateCopyBuffer()` call would leave the selection at a destination rows never reached, or paste from a stale buffer after a peer's structural edit.

samples.summary: The paste path's own merge-budget skip (`applyPasteMerges`) has no test
samples.evidence: `applyPasteMerges` spends a budget computed from the live map and `continue`s on blocks it cannot afford (sheet.ts:2763-2768) — the comment calls a paste 'the one gesture that adds many blocks at once, so it is where the map's budget is most easily overspent'. The new paste tests in merge.test.ts cover a store *refusal* (ToggleRefusingStore) but never a paste whose blocks exceed the engine-side budget, so the accumulate-as-you-go branch (budget.entries/coveredCells increments) is unexercised: a bug there would let a paste grow the map past what `rebuildMergeCoverMap` can walk, or drop merges a paste should have kept.

samples.summary: Entry-cap test asserts only the return value, not that nothing was written
samples.evidence: 'refuses once the map holds the entry cap' (lines 109-118) asserts only `setMerge(...) === false`; unlike its sibling tests it never reads back `merges()`, so a regression where the block is refused-but-still-queued to the document would pass. The adjacent covered-cell test (lines 120-128) does check the stored map.

samples.summary: The MaxSnappedFreeze release path is untested on the insert/delete route
samples.evidence: `snapFreezePastMerges` releasing the axis to 0 when the snap would exceed MaxSnappedFreeze is tested only through `setFreezePane` (merge.test.ts 'should release the freeze rather than snap past what the renderer paints') and by calling the helper directly. No test drives it through `shiftCells` (sheet.ts:1471-1483) or `applyWorksheetShift` (worksheet-structure.ts:278-287), where an insert/delete could newly trip the ceiling and silently unfreeze the tab; the two new workbook tests only cover the ordinary snap and the no-op case.

mergedFrom.summary: New merge-budget enforcement and batch merge overlay in YorkieStore have no test at all
Batched deleteMerge now consults the projected map instead of the document; no test covers delete-after-set-within-one-batch

finding.summary: The delta's real new logic — YorkieStore.setMerge budgeting, refusal, and the batchMerges/projectedMerges overlay — has no test anywhere
finding.evidence: This delta rewrites YorkieStore.setMerge to (a) spend the merge budget at call time against a projected map, (b) exclude the anchor's own existing span when re-anchoring, (c) return false on refusal, and (d) track queued writes in `batchMerges` so a paste's many blocks are budgeted against the map the batch is building. No test exercises any of it: grep for `setMerge|projectedMerges|batchMerges` matches no file under packages/frontend/tests (only src + sheets tests), and a case-insensitive grep for `merge` across packages/frontend/tests returns only docs/slides/utils tests. The sheets tests added here use MemStore subclasses whose setMerge is overridden wholesale, so they never touch the budget arithmetic. If the overlay or the self-exclusion is wrong, a paste can overspend the cap (storing a merge map a later load cannot walk) or silently drop a legal re-anchor — both data-affecting and invisible to the green suite.

verdict.reason:
A dedicated test file for exactly this behavior exists: packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store-merge-budget.test.ts (211 lines, 10 tests). The finding's core evidence claim — that grep for `setMerge|projectedMerges|batchMerges` matches no file under packages/frontend/tests — is false; that grep matches this file in this repo.

Each of the four behaviors the finding calls untested has a test:
(a) call-time budgeting against the projected map: tests at :101 (per-span cap), :109 (MaxMergeEntries cap), :120 (MaxMergeCoveredCells cap), seeded to exact cap boundaries using the real exported constants, exercising mergeBudgetOf/mergeBudgetAdmits at yorkie-store.ts:1019.
(b) self-exclusion when re-anchoring: "re-anchoring spends a block it does not add to" (:130-139) fills the map to the covered-cell cap then rewrites an existing anchor with an equally large span and asserts true — this fails if the `key !== sref` exclusion at yorkie-store.ts:1016-1017 is removed.
(c) refusal returned as false: asserted at :104, :115, :122, :159-166.
(d) batchMerges overlay: "budgets a block against the map the batch is building" (:143-173) queues ten cap-filling blocks in one batch and asserts the eleventh is refused AND absent from the flush, covering projectedMerges() at yorkie-store.ts:975-991 and batchMerges?.set at :1033; three further tests (:175-202) cover batch deletes freeing budget via yorkie-store.ts:1046-1048.

The test is not vacuous or over-mocked: it builds a real YorkieStore over a real unattached Yorkie Document (:47-63) and reads the actual CRDT root back as plain data (:68-80), asserting stored map contents plus return values. It is wired into the suite — vite.config.ts:375-380 includes tests/**/*.test.ts with no exclude — and no test is skipped.
